problem_statement: Write a program to check if a string is a palindrome, meaning it reads the same forward and backward. Given Input: str1 = \"radar\". Expected Output: Is Palindrome: True.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses whether the algorithm's logic accurately identifies palindromes and non-palindromes for all valid string inputs.
sub_criteria: The algorithm's comparison logic correctly determines if characters at symmetric positions in the string are identical.
The algorithm correctly concludes the string is *not* a palindrome if any character mismatch is found.
The algorithm correctly concludes the string *is* a palindrome if all symmetric character pairs match.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates if all essential structural components and necessary steps for the palindrome check are present in the pseudocode.
sub_criteria: The pseudocode describes taking a string as input.
The pseudocode includes a mechanism to systematically compare characters from both ends of the string moving inwards.
The pseudocode correctly handles edge cases such as empty strings or strings with a single character.
The pseudocode describes producing a final boolean result (True/False) indicating if the string is a palindrome.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: This dimension assesses how easily a human can understand the logical steps, intent, and flow of the pseudocode for checking palindromes.
sub_criteria: Each step of the palindrome checking process is described using clear and unambiguous language.
Any values, indices, or temporary storage used in the algorithm are clearly referenced and their purpose is understandable.
The overall sequence of operations and decision points is easy to follow.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: This dimension evaluates if the algorithm demonstrates an awareness of minimizing operations by avoiding redundant comparisons or unnecessary passes through the data.
sub_criteria: The algorithm stops comparisons as soon as a character mismatch is detected.
The algorithm avoids performing redundant operations or making multiple full passes over the string when a single pass (or half-pass) is sufficient.
